zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two or more attribute values (e.g., "Alice is the person with blonde hair"), treat them as a single combined entity and propagate that equivalence throughout the reasoning.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states that two attributes refer to the same house/person.
zebralogic.example: Assigning "Alice" to house 1 and "blonde hair" to house 2 separately, ignoring that they must be together.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "The jazz lover is in the sixth house"), record that assignment right away and use it to restrict other attributes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains an explicit house index.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring that "jazz is house 6" and later placing jazz elsewhere.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Adjacency clues ('next to', 'directly left of', 'directly right of') require the two referenced houses to be immediate neighbors; they are not satisfied by any non‑adjacent ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses "directly left of", "directly right of", or "next to".
zebralogic.example: Placing A at house 1 and B at house 3 for a clue "A is directly left of B".

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The verifier expects a JSON object with a "header" array listing column names and a "rows" array of rows; any deviation causes a parsing failure.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the final step, before returning the answer.
zebralogic.example: Returning a plain‑text table instead of the required JSON object.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: The model has a limited token budget; overly long reasoning can cause the final JSON to be cut off, leading to an incomplete answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the reasoning, keep explanations brief and place the final JSON at the end.
zebralogic.example: Writing a multi‑page step‑by‑step derivation before the JSON, causing the JSON to be omitted.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be reproduced exactly as given (including case, spaces, punctuation); any deviation leads to a mismatch with the reference solution.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON rows.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: For clues containing "somewhere to the right of" or "somewhere to the left of", enforce a strict ordering (the referenced house must be to the right/left, but not necessarily adjacent).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses "somewhere to the left/right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "somewhere to the left of" as "directly left of" and forcing adjacency.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "Eric is not in the first house"), ensure that attribute is never placed there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negative placement.
zebralogic.example: Placing Eric in house 1 despite the clue that he cannot be there.

zebralogic.title: Transitive Ordering Inference
zebralogic.principle: When multiple direct ordering clues form a chain (e.g., A left of B and B left of C), infer the implied ordering (A left of C) and use it to narrow possible positions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After collecting all ordering clues, compute the transitive closure of the left‑of relations.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring that "pop left of Mediterranean" and "Mediterranean left of jazz" together imply "pop left of jazz".

zebralogic.title: Chain adjacency constraints into consecutive blocks
zebralogic.principle: When two or more adjacency clues share a house (e.g., A directly left of B and B directly left of C), they form a block of consecutive houses; treat the block as a unit and enforce that the houses occupy consecutive positions in the given order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever multiple adjacency clues involve overlapping houses, before assigning individual positions, combine them into a consecutive block.
zebralogic.example: Placing A at house 1, B at house 3, and C at house 4 for clues "A directly left of B" and "B directly left of C", which violates the required consecutive block.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be thorough and writes extensive step‑by‑step derivations, exceeding the token limit before the JSON is emitted.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning brief, place the final JSON at the very end, and limit intermediate text.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model outputs a plain table or a JSON structure that differs from the expected schema.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Follow the exact JSON schema with a "header" array and a "rows" array of rows.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes or capitalizes attribute strings, deviating from the exact tokens given in the puzzle.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values verbatim, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses "somewhere to the left of" with "directly left of" or reverses the direction of the ordering.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Distinguish between ordering clues (non‑adjacent) and adjacency clues; verify the intended direction before applying.

zebralogic.description: Treating adjacency clues as non‑adjacent ordering, leading to placement errors.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets "directly left of" or "directly right of" as merely "to the left/right of", allowing gaps between houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Enforce that adjacency clues require immediate neighbor positions (house X = house Y ± 1).
